answer: Latency decay registration. Each new identity pays a small fee, but its voting weight and message reach start near zero and rise along a fixed curve over hours; early actions route through a slower review queue. Attacker cost is the wall-clock time and parallel queue capacity needed to make N identities matter at once. The ivory ceiling of throughput caps burst leverage. A trellis of time-staggered slots forces coordination overhead. Honest newcomers simply wander in gradually, while mass-created identities stall.
